channel.title: Trend Reader
channel.description: The AI vocabulary, mapped: a weekly brief on the terms and themes to know, and every new term as it is defined.

item.title: Weekly brief, week W42: Maia 300, Muse Wonder
item.description: This week's terms: Maia 300, Muse Wonder. product · Compute & infrastructure

item.title: New term: Maia 300
item.description: Maia 300 is Microsoft's third-generation custom inference accelerator, announced for 2027 data centres with a company-reported 40 percent more tokens per watt than leading GPU-based systems. It matters because it commits the largest reseller of other companies' compute to serving its own products on its own silicon.

item.title: New term: Model welfare
item.description: Model welfare is the question of whether AI systems have interests that deserve consideration, and the practices a developer adopts in case they do. It matters because it has moved from philosophy into commercial terms of service and training practice, which makes it operational regardless of how the underlying question is settled.

item.title: New term: Muse Wonder
item.description: Muse Wonder is Meta's first frontier model family, released in October 2026 and claimed comparable to the leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic, with an emphasis on retaining personal information over time. It matters because it made Meta a frontier competitor roughly a year after the company was widely written off.

item.title: Newsletter: Frontier quality at mid-tier prices
item.description: On 22 September the cost of frontier-grade coding fell across two vendors on the same day. Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5.5 at $4 per million input tokens and $20 output, the first cut in the Opus line after four versions at $5 and $25, with cache reads 60 percent cheaper on top.
